title: Coworker, rambling: colleague's sentences fall apart mid-meeting, right arm drops, mouth sags

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: 911, what's the address of the emergency?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hi, yes, sorry, we're at Bayline Logistics, 600 Townsend Street, fourth floor. It's my coworker, Diane. I'm not family, I just sit next to her.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Okay. Tell me what's going on with Diane.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: So we were going over the quarterly numbers and halfway through a sentence she just started saying things that weren't real words, like a jumble, and then her right arm just slid off the keyboard and hung there.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Is she awake? Can she talk to you now?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: She's awake, she's looking at me, she's trying, but what comes out is nonsense. And the right corner of her mouth, it’s sagging down. I don't know if that's important.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: When did you last see her completely normal?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Um, she ran the whole meeting, she was totally sharp. The meeting ended at ten past three, I remember because I checked the clock. So she was fine at ten past three.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Do you know if she takes any medications, like blood thinners?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I have no idea, honestly. I can ask HR for her emergency contact?

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: That's okay. How old is she, roughly?

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Okay. Help is on the way. Keep her sitting and stay with her.
